summary: Iter-13 retest verified BOTH iter-12 findings are fixed. (a) HIGH lifespan migration landed: `from contextlib import asynccontextmanager` (line 49) + `@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(_app)` (lines 56-92) + `FastAPI(title='ERRORHACKER API', lifespan=lifespan)` (line 95). Lifespan body restores all unique + non-unique indexes (13 await db.*.create_index calls, exceeds the required ≥13) and logs 'ERRORHACKER API ready' on startup — confirmed in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log (2 recent reloads at 12:53:47 and 12:54:45 both show the INFO line). No `@app.on_event` decorators remain anywhere in server.py (only a docstring reference inside lifespan() itself). (b) MEDIUM PATCH /orders/{id} try/except isolation landed at lines 1823-1842: _notify_user_order, notify_order_status, and send_order_receipt_email each have their OWN `try: asyncio.create_task(...)` / `except Exception as e: log.warning('<fn> dispatch failed: %s', e)` block. Full regression suite: 52 PASS / 1 pre-existing iter-9 skip / 0 fail across iter-9, iter-10, iter-12 and the new iter-13 test file.
critical_code_review_comments: Lifespan implementation is clean and idiomatic — forward-references _ensure_config / _ensure_admin / db / client are intentional (resolved lazily at call time) and the start-up index creation is wrapped in try/except so duplicate-index errors on hot reload do not crash the worker.

PATCH /orders/{id} now matches the per-task isolation pattern already used in me_pay_with_wallet and _cashfree_reconcile — 3 separate try/except blocks, each emitting log.warning with the failing dispatch's name (great for grep-based ops debugging).

Behavioural smoke (admin token → POST /api/orders → PATCH status='verified' payment_amount=499) returns 200 OK and no dispatch-failed warnings were observed in the log window — confirming none of the 3 async tasks raised during normal flow.

Minor follow-up (NOT blocking): the docstring inside lifespan() includes the literal text 'deprecated @app.on_event handlers'. iter-12's overly-loose substring assertion `"on_event" not in src` initially failed because of this docstring. I tightened that test to use a regex matching only the actual `@<x>.on_event(` decorator pattern + a positive check for `lifespan=lifespan`. No production code change needed.
